The enemies sometimes do cover up projectiles, or your own projectiles cover up enemy projectiles. That can be a bit rough; however, the dodge and projectile speed allow you to still dodge if you just keep moving.
Even though it has a lot going on on screen, it runs even better than some of the pixel versions I have seen of these types of games.

So far, I think it really does this kind of horde fight game genre justice; the character not being human gives it a fun twist, and the ability mutation feature is amazing. Being able to adjust your abilities with not just one fixed upgrade path made it really feel like I got to choose my own playstyle.

SPOILER WARNING:

What I slightly disliked (nothing game-breaking) was the NPCs acting like I died on my first try. However, I managed to beat the first level on the very first try. And when I got to the NPCs, they still went, "I saved you after you died," and the big bad fire only gave me his first meeting dialogue. It was only acknowledged that I beat the warrior AFTER I failed the next run. I completely understand why it was done from a coding standpoint. It just felt a bit odd, as it slightly displaced the natural lore progression.

What I really liked however, was finding out on my own that just going close range wasn't going to work out on the second level, as the first mini-boss really gave me a run for my money. Having to prepare myself correctly after failing was great.

The first level being beatable when you first start the game was also amazing! It made me feel like I really earned it.

Sound:
No loud obnoxious noises, pleasant and upbeat. Fits the theme of the game well without being too "in your face"

It’s a pretty fun Vampire Survivors-like with some nice new features but the current content is still very sparse, since this is very Early Access. What is currently there is pretty polished and there’s a lot of potential for the game. Overall, I would recommend getting it for a casual fun time.

+ I like the addition of Encounters. It gives different things to do and keeps you moving to different locations instead of settling with a stationary build. There’s currently only three versions in the game right now but they’re pretty fun to do especially when they align with swarms.

+ There’s only two maps so far but I like the ‘stage hazard’ added with the second map. Movement is slippery due to the ice on the second map and it adds a nice level of difficulty and uniqueness to it.

+ I like the fire twink constantly taunting you.

= I like the art style. It’s very similar to Coral Island, which seems to be the devs’ style. It does make it a bit difficult to gauge enemies and environment sometimes since VS-type games seem to benefit from a simpler art style. Nothing too bad though.

= There are instances when minibosses get stuck in the geography but this is rare. I have seen this happen twice on the second map with the whale getting stuck under the ice arches. Not a bad bug since it’s a free kill and it doesn’t happen often.

= Sound design is pretty crisp. The skills sound satisfying, especially lightning and earth skills. The enemy sounds, especially in the first map, is very cartoony though which matches the artstyle I suppose, but it’s not my style.

- The difficulty doesn’t seem to be tuned very well at the moment as it’s too easy. Even with a high fire level, enemy damage is not that much of a threat since I don’t think I’ve seen them take off more than one heart (even in Hard). Would love to see more difficulty especially in Hard and above. It would really help replayability and exploration of different builds.

- Alert banners (like for minibosses) last quite long and obscure a huge part of the upper half of the screen. This could result in you getting killed, especially when they ramp up the difficulty. I think it should go away a bit faster or have lower opacity so that you aren’t blind to the enemies behind it.

Funguys Swarm, developed and published by Stairway Games, is a chaotic, fast-paced roguelite bullet hell that blends humor, action, and charm into a surprisingly addictive survival experience. Set in a whimsical forest overrun by fire-based enemies, the game tasks you with playing as a brave little mushroom—or “Funguy”—who must battle increasingly overwhelming waves of enemies while collecting upgrades, saving forest creatures, and gradually building a community. Beneath its cartoonish visuals and absurd premise lies a cleverly designed game that rewards creativity, experimentation, and reflexes in equal measure.

The gameplay loop is simple in structure but rich in execution. Each run begins with your chosen Funguy character armed with a weapon—anything from a Watermelon Axe to a Garlic Hammer—and thrown into a hostile arena. Waves of enemies, from possessed carrots to flame-throwing vegetation, swarm the screen as you dodge, attack, and collect power-ups. After each round, you're offered a choice of upgrades that radically affect your build, allowing for wild combinations of skills and weapons. It's in these moments that Funguys Swarm shines brightest. The freedom to mix and match upgrades results in unpredictable yet satisfying builds, encouraging players to experiment and improvise. No two runs feel the same, and the escalating chaos is where the game finds its rhythm.

What makes the experience even more compelling is the persistent progression system. As you rescue friendly forest creatures during runs, they return to your home base—known as the Sanctuary—where they unlock permanent upgrades and features. This loop between short-term roguelite chaos and long-term progression offers a sense of accomplishment even after failed attempts. It’s a rewarding system that balances challenge with accessibility, making each run feel like it’s contributing to something larger. The Sanctuary also gives the game a cozy narrative backbone, reminding players that there's a community worth fighting for amid the madness.

Visually, the game embraces a playful, vibrant art style that sets it apart from the often gritty or dark aesthetics of the genre. Characters are expressive, animations are bouncy, and each biome—from the Carrot Farm to the Frozen Pond—is rendered with charming detail. The contrast between the whimsical art and the intensity of bullet hell combat adds to the game’s unique identity. Sound design also contributes to the game’s energetic tone, with upbeat music and satisfying effects that enhance the action without overwhelming the senses. The user interface is colorful and functional, though it can feel slightly cluttered during heavy combat sequences—a common growing pain in early access titles.

Being an early access game, Funguys Swarm is still evolving. As of its launch, it features two characters, three core weapons, a growing list of skills, and a couple of biomes to explore. While content is currently limited compared to more mature roguelites, the foundation is strong, and the developer has already begun rolling out patches and responding to player feedback. A recent hotfix addressed issues with skill rerolling, UI responsiveness, and performance—demonstrating a clear commitment to iterative improvement. There are occasional hiccups, such as minor bugs or rare crashes, but nothing game-breaking or out of the ordinary for early access. The gameplay itself is stable, and the developers are transparent about their roadmap.

Community involvement is another highlight. The developers actively engage with players via feedback forums and update blogs, and future plans include more weapons, new enemies, additional biomes, and expanded story elements. There's also a fun bit of crossover for fans of Coral Island, another Stairway Games project, with unlockable cosmetic items that connect the two universes. This shared-world approach is a subtle but effective way to build brand identity and community loyalty.

While it may not yet have the sheer volume of content found in giants of the genre like Vampire Survivors or Hades, Funguys Swarm is clearly on the path to becoming something special. It combines the frenetic joy of bullet hell shooters with the satisfying depth of roguelite progression, all wrapped in a charming, forest-fantasy aesthetic that feels refreshing in a genre that can often take itself too seriously. For players who enjoy quick sessions, chaotic build variety, and quirky humor with surprising depth, Funguys Swarm is an easy recommendation—especially for those who appreciate being part of a game’s journey from its early roots to full bloom.

[h1]Fungi, Fun, and Flawless Fun: Why Funguys: Swarm is the Next Big Survivor[/h1]

In the ever-growing genre of "survivor-like" games, it's becoming increasingly difficult to stand out. So many titles have attempted to replicate the addictive, minimalist magic of Vampire Survivors, often with mixed results. Enter Funguys: Swarm, an early access title from Stairway Games that not only embraces the formula but injects it with such personality and polish that it carves out its own delightful, fungus-filled niche.

At its core, Funguys: Swarm will feel immediately familiar to anyone who has played a "survivor" game. You control a character who automatically attacks a relentless, ever-growing horde of enemies. The goal is to survive, level up, and build an absurdly overpowered character by combining upgrades and abilities. But while the DNA is the same, the execution is what makes this game feel so fresh.

The moment you start your first run, the game's vibrant world bursts to life. The levels are not just generic backgrounds but are full of character, from the lush, verdant foliage of the forest floor to the whimsical, mutated foes that fill the screen. The visuals are a stunning and joyful departure from the often grim or retro aesthetics of its contemporaries. Each Funguys hero and every enemy, from fiery chilli peppers to menacing pomegrenades, is a work of art, with unique and expressive designs that make the chaotic combat a visual treat.

Beyond its striking looks, Funguys: Swarm innovates on the core formula in clever ways. The upgrade system feels more deliberate and impactful. The game's "Encounter" mechanic encourages exploration and offers unique challenges that can change the course of a run, moving the game beyond a simple "survive-in-one-spot" approach. Boss fights are a highlight, feeling like proper, escalating battles rather than just stat-check encounters. Most importantly, the game’s meta-progression in the Forest Sanctuary is incredibly satisfying, giving you permanent upgrades that genuinely make you feel more powerful with each new attempt.

Funguys: Swarm proves that the "survivor" genre is far from exhausted. It's a game that takes a proven recipe, adds its own unique and flavorful ingredients, and serves up a dish that's both comforting and exciting. It's addicting, charming, and genuinely fun. For a game still in Early Access, the level of polish and clear vision is impressive. If you're looking for your next "one more run" obsession, or if you've grown tired of the same old monster-slaying grind, this is the perfect game to get lost in.

pros:
- eventhough it's still early access, I haven't found any bug yet and never have an error so it's very stable and looks promising
- the skills we can pick every level up are randomized so it's fun to try each one of them and combine them to get our best strategy
- artstyle and sound design? chef kiss the visual is top level despite it's only 2.7gb
- tbh once I enter the map and start playing (I used the garlic hammer since it's automatically attacks the enemies) I only used mouse to pick the skills so it's very laptop friendly and perfect to play on the go when travelling
- I didn't feel any dizziness and felt perfectly fine even though I get motion sickness easily and sensitive towards fast-paced navigation in games, so it's a big green flag

cons:
- needs lots of time to get used to play it since there are many skills and we don't know what it does until we use it
- the skills randomizer sometimes doesn't play fair, you can get all heavenly skills in one round game and in another just okay-skills, so it's a bit annoying when you have bad luck
- might feel repetitive for some people since we basically play the same map and fight against the same enemy again and again, and it took lots of time to unlock a new map to play in (I think we can only unlock it once we defeat the current map's boss)
- sometimes the monsters attacks that reduce our heart can't be seen from too many monsters around us so it's kinda annoying, hope the developer will repair it in the full ver. game

I've been looking around for more Vampire Survivors-like games and I've played quite a few of them these last few years, this one is probably on my list of recommendations. As of now, with the 0.2 Update, there are 3 stages, Normal and Hard difficulties, 2 characters, 4 weapons, and a decent amount of upgrades for the overall game play. It gives you enough content to kill a couple of hours at best, however, once you get all the upgrades from the Shroom Store and the Dewpond, all there's left to do is grind for Amber to upgrade your weapons as well as Potatoes to grind for the Mech Upgrades added in the recent update.

It'd be nice if they add in either extra tiers for the Shroom Shop or allow Character Based upgrades, using the Shrooms as the currency, you have two Pets that you can bring along as well, allowing them to have upgrades that can be swapped around would bring some more variety to the game. Overall it's a good game, naturally as it is in Early Access there isn't a LOT of content, you can kill a couple hours or so and have a good time, but once more content and updates are made up to it's 1.0 Release, I think this will end up being a good Survivors-Like Game.

I’ve been playing Funguys Swarm for over five hours now, and honestly, I’m having a great time with it. The game is fast, colorful, and a little chaotic in the best way. Runs are quick but addictive — it’s always “just one more round” before I realize how much time has passed.

The art style is super cute and goofy, which makes the constant swarms of enemies feel fun instead of stressful. I really enjoy experimenting with different weapons and skills, and there’s a good amount of variety already even though it’s still in Early Access. Unlocking new characters and rescuing creatures between runs adds a nice sense of progress.

Performance-wise, it runs smoothly on my PC without any issues. For the price, I think it’s a fantastic deal, and I’m excited to see how the developers expand it with more maps and upgrades.

Overall, Funguys Swarm feels polished, fun, and easy to recommend if you like survivor-style games like Vampire Survivors. Can’t wait to see where it goes from here!

+3% damage for one type of skills?
3% chance to summon an ability when you are attacking (every 2.5 sec) ?..
Slightly reduce cooldown of your attacks when you dash (ever 6 sec) ?..
The strongest upgrade that you can level up to a maximum during the run is +25% attack speed for ONE weapon.
